 tweaking your daily food intake by making small heart-
healthy choices can accumulate to make a big difference in the long
run (table 2.1). The American Heart Association (AHA, www.heart.org)
recommends enjoying a healthy eating pattern that is rich in vegetables,
fruits, and whole-grain, high-fiber foods. You can enhance your eating
pattern with the following diet and lifestyle choices to reduce your risk of
cardiovascular disease:

© Reaching or maintaining a healthy weight

* Consuming at least 7 ounces (200 g) of oily fish per week

* Limiting your intake of saturated fat and partially hydrogenated oils

* Replacing saturated animal fat with healthy unsaturated fat from nuts,

avocados, and plant oils

* Limiting your intake of beverages and foods with added sugars to

control your weight

* Choosing and preparing foods with little or no salt

* Consuming alcohol in moderation (if at all)

* Making reasonably healthy choices when you dine away from home

* Being active for at least 30 minutes most days of the week
